subject: Console export: 'replay window' for route-level cost/latency playback
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Zoe Tan <zoe.tan@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Console export: 'replay window' for route-level cost/latency playback

Hi team,

Quick ask from SRE/CS (cc Zoe) after a cost spike last week: would it be possible to add a lightweight, exportable "replay window" feature in Console that lets customers export a time-bounded set of route-level requests and metadata so they can locally replay or share with us for forensic analysis?

What they want (high level):
- Pick a time range (e.g., 10:15–10:45 PST) and an endpoint/route.
- Export a CSV/NDJSON that contains per-request IDs, timestamp, route name, client-id, token_count (input/output), approximate cost estimate, latency_ms, and a hash pointer to request/response bodies (not raw PII).
- Optionally include full request/response bodies if customer has enabled export consent (toggle) — for Acme they can enable it.

Primary use cases:
1) Customer replay in dev to reproduce logs/latency regressions.
2) Our support team can import the small bundle into a replay harness to reproduce KV-cache effects and validate fallback behavior.
3) Quick billing / unit-cost investigations without spinning up full tracing export.

Constraints I expect: this shouldn't stream full payloads by default (privacy), and we should cap export size (e.g., 10k rows) and surface an estimate of file size / cost before export.

Attached a short proposal and a sample-export.csv with the column names we discussed. Would love product + infra feasibility notes and a rough timeline (MVP vs. full export) so I can feed back to Acme.

Thanks —
Elliot
Elliot Price | Senior Infra PM
Redwood Inference
elliot_price@redwood.com

Attachments: replay-proposal.pdf, sample-export.csv

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Zoe Tan <zoe.tan@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 12:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Console export: 'replay window' for route-level cost/latency playback

Thanks for the write-up, Elliot — this is a sensible customer-facing capability. A few clarifying questions before we scope:

1) Privacy & consent: if we include bodies, do we require explicit org-level consent + an audit event? If so, we should wire to the Private Export toggle in Console and record the export actor (sensitive).
2) Level of fidelity: do customers need full KV cache state to reproduce tail latency, or is request/resp + token_count enough for 90% of cases? Acme suggests they want cache impacts captured.
3) UX: do we build this as an "Export" button on the route timeline (quick) + a background job with download link, or a new "Replay" tab that lets you trigger a test replay in a sandbox?

Initial proposal: MVP = export CSV/NDJSON with the fields Elliot listed, with body hashes and an optional ORG-level consent flag to include payloads. No cache state for MVP (we can add a cache snapshot later). If engineering agrees, target: alpha in ~6 weeks, beta in 12.

Kimberly/Marissa — tagging you for engineering effort and infra safety checks (rate, quota, retention of exported bundles). Also marking OBS-9421 for tracking.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Product Manager, Observability
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Console export: 'replay window' for route-level cost/latency playback

Looping in engineering constraints — thanks for framing this. A couple of notes from infra side:

- KV cache state: capturing precise KV cache contents is expensive and fragile across prod replicas. For reproducibility we can capture a cache-miss fingerprint (cache_key, miss_count) but not the full cache dump in MVP.
- Token-cost calculation: we can include the token counts we store (input_tokens, output_tokens) and a matching per-token price used in cost calculations; that will allow a deterministic "approx cost" column. Exact invoice-level reconciliation requires the billing pipeline but this is usually sufficient for forensics.
- Export scale & rate limits: background job should cap at 10k rows per export; larger requests must be paginated and gated by quota. We'll surface estimated S3 size and retention TTL (default 7 days).
- Sensitive data: default export must redact PII; payload inclusion must be an explicit org-level opt-in and logged.

I've created a tracking ticket and technical spike: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-9421 (initial estimate: 5 dev-weeks for MVP + a 1-week infra rollout). We should discuss whether the same export code path powers a future "replay-in-sandbox" feature or if replay will be done offline by customers.

I can take the spike this week and pair with Marissa on UX and retention defaults.

-Kim

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for creating OBS-9421. A few notes from Acme's SRE team that would make the export most useful for us:

- Please include request_id, request_timestamp, route, client_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_estimate_usd, latency_ms, and a response_hash column. The sample-export.csv you attached looks great.
- For replays we don't need full payloads in most cases; the response_hash + ability to request payloads (with org consent) is fine.
- It would be incredibly helpful if the export included a mapping to our tracing IDs (we send x-acme-trace-id as a header) so we can crosswalk with our traces.

If helpful, we can share a small set of anonymized logs for your spike. Happy to schedule a 30-minute sync this week if you want to walk through end-to-end.

Cheers,
Zoe Tan | Senior SRE, Acme Corp
zoe.tan@acme.com
